newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach hauled before select committee.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach hauled before select committee.

text.p: Stagecoach Holdings Plc, the company behind South West Trains which has cancelled and delayed dozens of peak-time services since taking over, has been called to explain itself to the UK parliament's transport select committee next week.

Brian Cox, managing director of the rail franchise responsible called South West Trains, is due to give evidence to the cross-party committee next Wednesday and will be questioned about the collapse in peak services which has seen scores of cancellations.
A spokesman for the select committee announced the move and Stagecoach confirmed Cox would make an appearance.

The news comes amid reports that Stagecoach could be fined less than 300,000 pounds by the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf), which was not available for comment. But last week Opraf told Reuters Stagecoach would be fined tens of thousands of pounds but would not give further details.
Stagecoach has been forced to reduce services drastically after axing too many drivers in a cost-cutting drive which has now backfired.

In a bid to make amends with disillusioned passengers, Stagecoach offered them a free day's travel. But with some customers taking the advantage of asking for trips as far afield as France, the full cost of this public relations exercise is unclear.
